subject: Fungal and bacterial transformation of artemisinin and other antimalarial terpenoids produced derivative candidates
scope_note: transformed or engineered derivatives are not native Artemisia metabolites and require independent efficacy and safety testing

subject: Review of carbon-radical, heme, activation, combination, and competing mechanistic hypotheses for artemisinin antimalarials
scope_note: supports explicit mechanism uncertainty and multi-target framing; no sole parasite target is established

subject: Fifteen Lithuanian wild populations yielded davanone, germacrene-D, 1,8-cineole, camphor, thujone, and chrysanthenyl-acetate oil profiles; brine-shrimp LC0 values were 10.3-23.1 microgram/mL
scope_note: population-level volatile variation and brine-shrimp toxicity do not predict mammalian safety or a single constituent effect

subject: AaDBR2 and feverfew CYP71CB1 accepted multiple sesquiterpene substrates and enabled engineered dihydrocostunolide and dihydroparthenolide production
scope_note: supports catalytic plasticity as an evolutionary opportunity; heterologous production is not evidence of native pathway flux or antiparasitic activity

subject: Review of transcription factors and structural genes that jointly regulate artemisinin and flavonoid biosynthesis
scope_note: supports co-regulation and matrix hypotheses; shared regulation does not prove terpene-flavonoid synergy

subject: Crude methanolic flower and leaf extracts produced concentration- and time-dependent adult-motility and egg-hatch inhibition against Haemonchus contortus; flower extract reached 98.67% egg-hatch inhibition at 1 mg/mL
scope_note: comparative crude-extract in-vitro evidence; active constituent, host selectivity, and translation to A. absinthium or humans remain unresolved

subject: Salt, cold, drought, and waterlogging altered transcriptomes and artemisinin content; drought was the exception to the reported increase
scope_note: stress response is treatment- and genotype-context-specific and does not establish universal ecological regulation or safe production

subject: Arsenic stress and carrageenan oligomer plus salicylic-acid treatment altered oxidative physiology and increased artemisinin yield in two varieties
scope_note: supports an environment-by-regulation hypothesis in tested varieties; it is not parasite efficacy or a general production recommendation

subject: Cultivated wormwood yielded absilactone, hansonlactone, ajenjol, and 3α-hydroxypelenolide; fungal transformation and acid rearrangement generated additional products
scope_note: expands structurally characterized wormwood STL chemistry; insect antifeedant and Sf9 cytotoxicity endpoints do not establish anthelmintic efficacy

subject: Eight A. argyi oil volatiles were rapidly absorbed and distributed mainly to rat liver, heart, kidney, lung, and spleen before prompt elimination
scope_note: rat exposure data inform disposition hypotheses but do not establish parasite efficacy, target engagement, or a safe human dose

subject: One liter of tea prepared from 9 g leaves produced mean artemisinin Cmax 240 +/- 75 ng/mL and AUC 336 +/- 71 ng/mL*h in 14 healthy men
scope_note: human tea exposure is a matrix-specific PK anchor; the study did not establish equivalence to modern artemisinin drugs

subject: Soaking or pounding fresh Qing Hao produced extracts up to 20-fold more concentrated than dried-herb tea; only pounded juice suppressed P. berghei parasitemia
scope_note: concentration and total extracted dose diverged; preparation is not standardized clinical therapy

subject: Dried whole plant containing 24 mg/kg artemisinin reduced P. chabaudi parasitemia more than equal pure drug and was associated with approximately 40-fold higher mouse bioavailability
scope_note: preclinical matrix effect; synergistic constituents and clinical translation remain unresolved

subject: Tea and nonpolar extract IC50 values against P. falciparum closely followed artemisinin concentration and did not differ significantly from pure artemisinin
scope_note: one in-vitro preparation and strain context; does not exclude matrix effects in other models

subject: Dried-leaf artemisinin AUC was 299.5 mg*min/L in healthy mice versus 435.6 mg*min/L in P. chabaudi-infected mice and deoxyartemisinin metabolism was suppressed
scope_note: infection and plant matrix alter exposure; no direct protein target or human dose is established

subject: 5 g DW/L teas inhibited P. falciparum asexual and early/late gametocytes; effects were mainly artemisinin-dependent with a weak artemisinin-deficient A. afra signal
scope_note: stage-resolved in-vitro extract result; constituent attribution and clinical transmission impact remain unresolved

subject: Dried-leaf extracts showed time- and strain-dependent P. falciparum activity and malaria-patient sera enhanced inhibition in some assays
scope_note: possible host interaction is a hypothesis; crude extract and serum effects do not identify a terpene target

subject: Low-concentration infusions inhibited blood and liver stages including P. vivax and P. cynomolgi hypnozoites in vitro and were reported as essentially artemisinin-independent
scope_note: active chemistry and clinical relevance are unresolved; unregulated plant remedies remain a suboptimal-therapy concern

subject: All tested teas inhibited human CYP2B6 and CYP3A4 activity; high-artemisinin tea induced transcription while artemisinin-deficient teas did not
scope_note: supports post-transcriptional phytochemical interaction risk, not parasite efficacy or safe posology

subject: Dried leaves increased artemisinin tissue exposure in rats and inhibited CYP2B6/CYP3A4 in human liver microsomes
scope_note: responsible phytochemical(s), sex effects, and human translation remain unresolved

subject: Aqueous extract caused dose-dependent paralysis, death, tegumental damage, and reduced EPG and worm burden for H. nana in vitro and infected mice
scope_note: stronger than a purely folkloric claim but crude-extract chemistry and human efficacy are unresolved

subject: Seven-day 300 or 600 mg/kg extract dosing reduced Toxocara cati fecal egg counts in naturally infected cats while egg embryonation was unaffected in vitro
scope_note: veterinary phenotype with a negative egg-development result; requires replication and constituent attribution

subject: Aqueous and ethanolic extracts completely inhibited H. contortus egg hatching near 2 mg/mL; ethanolic extract caused 100% adult mortality at the highest 24-h dose
scope_note: extract chemistry was flavonoid-dominated, so the phenotype is not terpene evidence

subject: Methanolic extracts at 50 mg/mL produced egg-hatch inhibition of 85 +/- 21.2% and 80 +/- 28.3% respectively but lower larval and adult mortality
scope_note: in-vitro comparative signal; purification and in-vivo confirmation were not completed

subject: n-Hexane extract showed 75% and 82.6% activity against H. contortus L3 at 1 and 2 mg/mL; isoguaiacine and extract altered Hc29 expression and extract reduced gerbil infection 100%
scope_note: expression change is not direct binding; extract chemistry, host selectivity, and reproducibility remain open

subject: Two haplotype genome maps and 36 resequenced samples supported a correlation between ADS copy number and artemisinin content
scope_note: copy-number correlation is a strong prioritization signal but not causal proof or cross-species pathway equivalence

subject: Commentary on the interpretation of chemical analyses and anthelmintic effects of A. campestris essential oil
scope_note: no abstract and no new quantitative result; retained for interpretation audit

subject: Powdered shoots were administered to six experimentally infected goats at 2, 10, or 30 g and most treated goats showed absent fecal eggs and no adult worms at necropsy, with incomplete suppression in two
scope_note: older small goat study; chemistry, standardized dose, and replication remain open

subject: Historical preliminary report screening wormwood against P. berghei in mice
scope_note: title and metadata only because no abstract was available; not used for quantitative inference

subject: Historical report on artemisinin in traditional A. annua tea preparations
scope_note: title and metadata only because no abstract was available; not used for quantitative inference

subject: Thirteen-week rat exposure to 0.125, 0.5, or 2% wormwood extract found no obvious treatment-related toxicity and estimated a study-specific NOAEL at or above 1.27 g/kg/day in males and 2.06 g/kg/day in females
scope_note: rat extract result does not define human safety, thujone exposure, or safety of other chemotypes

subject: Aqueous powder suspensions of A. annua but not A. afra showed antimalarial activity in P. berghei-infected mice
scope_note: negative in-vivo A. afra result constrains interpretation of artemisinin-independent in-vitro activity; not human efficacy

subject: Ethyl-acetate extract produced greater than 60% ovicidal activity against F. hepatica above 300 mg/L and adult-fluke activity at tested concentrations
scope_note: comparative extract and artemisinin record; active constituent and host selectivity unresolved

subject: Peruvin binary mixtures with 1-nonacosanol/hentriacontane or cinic acid increased lethal effects against H. contortus L3 by 1.42-fold and 4.87-fold at matched LC25 proportions
scope_note: defined mixture result supports pair-specific synergy; host exposure and broader mixture reproducibility remain untested

subject: Aqueous white-wormwood extracts at 5 and 10 mg/mL immobilized or killed mature H. contortus in vitro, with complete killing at one tested treatment after 6 h
scope_note: adult-worm in-vitro result; no in-vivo efficacy, chemistry resolution, or terpene attribution

subject: Ethanolic extract caused 81.79% larval motility inhibition and 82.2% larvicidal activity at 200 mg/mL in vitro but did not significantly reduce FECRT in free-grazing goats at 600 mg/kg
scope_note: important negative in-vivo translation control; small regional study and unstandardized extract

subject: A. vulgaris extract reduced F. gigantica egg hatching to 3.33% at 5% concentration by day 16 and reached 66.67% adult-fluke mortality at 20% after 40 min
scope_note: in-vitro extract and morphology evidence; active compounds and mechanism remain unresolved

subject: Bioguided fractionation isolated eupatilin and a trimethoxylated flavone with activity against L. major promastigotes or amastigotes and low macrophage toxicity
scope_note: compound-level parasite evidence is non-terpene-centered and requires independent pharmacology

subject: Hydrotrope-assisted extracts yielded up to 6.50 or 6.44 mg/g artemisinin and showed greater P. falciparum activity than pure artemisinin in the tested system
scope_note: solvent and matrix effects confound causal assignment; not a clinical botanical regimen

subject: Blue and yellow light altered glandular-trichome anatomy, volatile diversity, ADS expression, and artemisinin accumulation in controlled plantlets
scope_note: controlled treatment association informs environment-by-chemotype hypotheses but not universal cultivation guidance

subject: Seventeen A. annua bioecotypes were compared by gene-specific STS markers and HPLC; polymorphic markers correlated with artemisinin yield and high-yield bioecotypes exceeded 2.7 mg/g dry weight
scope_note: marker correlations support selection within the sampled material but do not establish causal alleles or cross-environment stability

subject: AaSPATULA overexpression increased glandular secretory-trichome density, artemisinin accumulation, leaf expansion, and biomass while RNAi reduced growth and artemisinin
scope_note: regulatory perturbation supports a trichome-yield link but pathway effects and genotype-by-environment transfer require validation

subject: Essential-oil profiles differed by geography and phenological stage with shifts among oxygenated monoterpenes, oxygenated sesquiterpenes, and monoterpene hydrocarbons
scope_note: site and stage effects establish chemotype stratification but do not identify stable taxon-wide markers or antiparasitic actives

subject: A low-thujone wormwood oil was dominated by trans-sabinyl acetate while trans-thujone was negligible and extracts contained phenolic acids and flavonoids
scope_note: low-thujone chemistry is product- and accession-specific and cannot be inferred from the species name alone

subject: Authenticated and commercial oils formed distinct thujone/camphor/ocimene-epoxide chemotype clusters and major thujones affected tephritid behavior and toxicity endpoints
scope_note: commercial-product variability and insect endpoints do not directly define human safety or vermifuge efficacy

subject: A validated LC-MS method quantified artemisinin at a 0.22 ng/mL limit of detection and separated genuine low abundance from likely cross-contamination in A. afra material
scope_note: analytical detection is necessary for provenance and dosing but does not establish biological activity or clinical quality

subject: A standardized A. annua extract showed activity against L. infantum promastigotes and amastigotes without RAW264.7 cytotoxicity and altered inflammatory cytokine readouts
scope_note: standardized-extract activity remains mixture-level and requires chemical fingerprinting, target studies, and in-vivo confirmation

subject: A. cina aqueous-extract silver nanoparticles increased H. contortus L3 mortality and altered antioxidant-enzyme readouts, but the tested entity was a nanoparticle formulation, not native plant extract or an isolated terpene
scope_note: nanoparticle synthesis and surface chemistry confound attribution to A. cina constituents and limit direct comparison with vermifuge preparations

subject: A Saudi A. absinthium oil was dominated by cis-davanone with additional sesquiterpenes and showed low cytotoxicity in the reported cell assay
scope_note: one regional oil and assay panel cannot define species-wide safety or anthelmintic mechanism

subject: TrichomeLess Regulator 3 affected glandular-trichome initiation, cuticle biosynthesis, and artemisinin-associated phenotypes in A. annua
scope_note: regulator perturbation connects tissue architecture to specialized metabolism but not directly to parasite phenotype

subject: JA-induced AaMYC3 increased glandular-trichome density and artemisinin biosynthesis and activated or interacted with upstream and pathway genes
scope_note: transcriptional regulation is a plant-side mechanism and requires metabolite-resolved parasite testing

subject: Differential lncRNAs were associated with ADS, DXS, HMGS, and other pathway genes in high- versus low-artemisinin material
scope_note: association-based lncRNA evidence does not establish direct regulation or evolutionary conservation

subject: Extraction comparisons identified solvent and process tradeoffs for recovery of artemisinin, dihydroartemisinin, and artemisinic acid, with acetonitrile high-performing and ethanol more practical for scale-up
scope_note: process recovery is not equivalent to bioavailability, efficacy, or safety and must be linked to a defined product fingerprint

subject: Animal-health literature supports interest in A. annua and artemisinin but emphasizes standardization and species-appropriate evidence
scope_note: review context does not substitute for primary parasite assays or establish a terpene-specific veterinary indication

subject: LED spectrum, macronutrients, and culture conditions altered biomass and artemisinin production in A. annua suspension cultures
scope_note: controlled culture effects support process-development hypotheses but not field-level chemotype predictions

subject: Copper toxicity reduced glandular-trichome traits and artemisinin-associated phenotypes, while exogenous ABA ameliorated cellular stress and increased trichome density and artemisinin production
scope_note: stress-hormone rescue is treatment-specific and does not establish a stable field chemotype or parasite phenotype

subject: TAR1 perturbation altered trichome morphology, cuticular wax composition, pathway-gene expression, and artemisinin content, with ADS and CYP71AV1 identified as likely direct targets
scope_note: direct promoter regulation and metabolite change are plant-side evidence; cross-species conservation and parasite effects remain open

subject: Trichome-specific AaWRKY1 overexpression increased CYP71AV1 transcription and artemisinin by about 1.8-fold without significant FDS ADS or DBR2 transcript changes
scope_note: promoter and transgene context limit inference about native allele effects or evolutionary divergence

subject: AabHLH1 bound E-box elements in ADS and CYP71AV1 promoters and activated pathway-associated transcription in transient assays
scope_note: binding and transactivation do not quantify native flux or establish conserved function in other Artemisia species

subject: DBR2 overexpression increased artemisinin and dihydroartemisinic acid but also increased arteannuin B and artemisinic acid in independent transgenic lines
scope_note: pathway engineering can raise competing branches as well as target product; it is not a simple one-enzyme yield rule

subject: Rhizophagus intraradices colonization increased jasmonic acid, glandular-trichome density, MEP-pathway signals, and artemisinin; matched JA levels reduced differences between mycorrhizal and control plants
scope_note: microbiome and hormone effects are context-dependent and require replicated environmental and chemical validation

subject: AaEIN3 overexpression promoted leaf senescence and suppressed ADS DBR2 CYP71AV1 and artemisinin, whereas RNAi enhanced pathway output
scope_note: developmental regulation does not by itself establish evolutionary change or parasite potency

subject: AaSPL2 activated the DBR2 promoter through a GTAC element; overexpression increased artemisinin 33-86% and RNAi decreased it 33-65%
scope_note: transgenic effect sizes are construct- and background-dependent and do not predict species-wide yield

subject: AabZIP9 bound ACGT elements in ADS and CYP71AV1 promoters and increased ADS, artemisinin, dihydroartemisinic acid, and artemisinic acid in transgenic plants
scope_note: promoter binding and product accumulation do not establish direct evolutionary homology or antiparasitic activity

subject: GT-free leaves and calli and a glandless mutant produced artemisinin, artemisinic acid, arteannuin B, and localized products in non-glandular cells
scope_note: revises a glandular-trichome-only model but remains specific to inbred and mutant material

subject: Combined UV-B and gibberellin treatments increased artemisinin and induced ADS/CYP71AV1 with co-expression modules enriched for candidate MYB and NAC regulators
scope_note: co-expression and treatment response identify candidate hubs, not direct regulation or transferable cultivation rules

subject: Artemisinin was highest in leaves at 0.343 mg/g, followed by flowers, roots, and stems, while upstream and pathway genes showed tissue-specific expression patterns
scope_note: bulk-tissue expression is not secretory-cell flux and the reported accession is not a genus-wide tissue profile

subject: Constitutive CO overexpression advanced flowering by about two weeks without increasing artemisinin, indicating that flowering time alone does not explain seasonal accumulation
scope_note: developmental timing and artemisinin accumulation are correlated but not directly interchangeable

subject: Field germplasms showed large seasonal and chemotype differences in artemisinin, dihydroartemisinic acid, and artemisinic acid; ART and DHAA often peaked before flowering
scope_note: harvest and germplasm effects support selection hypotheses but not pooled species means

subject: Eighteen populations included diploids and tetraploids, but neither ploidy class contained detectable artemisinin and DBR2 was low or silenced in autotetraploid material
scope_note: negative detection and expression comparison constrain artemisinin-equivalence claims but do not prove complete pathway absence

subject: Artemisinin inhibited recombinant TgSERCA activity and induced calcium-dependent microneme secretion and calcium perturbation in T. gondii
scope_note: supports a parasite Ca2+-ATPase target class outside malaria but does not establish a species-specific Artemisia preparation or sole mechanism

subject: Bioassay-guided fractionation identified 1alpha,4alpha-dihydroxybishopsolicepolide and yomogiartemin as principal A. afra gametocytocidal sesquiterpene lactone leads
scope_note: isolated-lactone activity strengthens constituent attribution but target engagement, host selectivity, and in-vivo transmission effects remain open

subject: Among 13 medicinal-plant extracts, methanolic A. absinthium was one of the most effective preparations against H. contortus eggs and larvae; the study also quantified selected phenolics but did not resolve terpene causality
scope_note: comparative extract result and phenolic measurements do not identify the active wormwood terpene or establish in-vivo efficacy

subject: Alcoholic A. absinthium extract showed concentration-dependent anti-embryogenic and anthelmintic effects against Ascaris suum eggs and developing larvae in a six-plant comparison; reported chemistry included sesquiterpene lactones and non-terpene metabolites
scope_note: in-vitro extract phenotype with mixed chemistry; active constituent, parasite target, and translation to mammalian treatment remain unresolved

subject: Isolation from A. nitrosa characterized one new germacrane-type sesquiterpene lactone, ten known sesquiterpenes, and a dimer using MS and multidimensional NMR; the isolated sesquiterpenoids lacked significant activity in the reported macrophage assay
scope_note: structure-confirmed chemistry and a negative non-parasitic bioassay do not establish an antiparasitic constituent or genus-wide chemotype

subject: Leaf fractionation isolated and characterized sesquiterpene lactones and a flavonoid from basin big sagebrush with structure and biological-activity analyses
scope_note: subspecies- and leaf-specific isolation record; non-parasitic activity does not transfer to wormwood or define a parasite mechanism

subject: Ethanolic aerial-part extraction yielded twelve new and ten known guaianolide sesquiterpene lactones with NMR, ECD, and crystallographic stereochemical support; isolated compounds inhibited macrophage NO production in vitro
scope_note: structure-activity and macrophage results are not antiparasitic evidence and cannot be assigned to all A. vulgaris or Artemisia material

subject: Whole-plant isolation yielded seven new sesquiterpenoids and nineteen known analogues, including uncommon skeletons and eudesmanolide lactones with extensive spectroscopic and stereochemical characterization
scope_note: structural novelty and anti-inflammatory screening broaden STL space but do not establish antiparasitic activity or pathway homology

subject: Integrated metabolomics, transcriptomics, and gene-function analysis identified 88 metabolites across 14 tissues, including 26 monoterpenes, 22 sesquiterpenes, two triterpenes, and one diterpene, and linked tissue/developmental expression patterns to terpene pathways
scope_note: single-species multi-tissue network and expression correlations do not establish comparative evolution or causal flux for every gene-metabolite pair

subject: An 8.03-Gb A. argyi assembly was reported as allotetraploid with extensive secondary-metabolism gene expansion, including 135 TPS genes with tandem clusters and tissue-biased expression
scope_note: assembly, ploidy, and annotation context differ from later A. argyi resources; gene-family expansion is not equivalent to intact function or metabolite flux

subject: A library of natural ADS/BFS sequence combinations identified an epistatic residue network that controls the emergence of terpene cyclization
scope_note: sequence-function landscape in A. annua supports testable TPS evolution; it does not establish ancestral states or native ecological selection across Artemisia

subject: High-speed countercurrent chromatography completely removed santonin from a CO2 subcritical A. cina extract; the santonin-free extract and pectolinarigenin retained antinociceptive/anti-inflammatory activity
scope_note: santonin removal changes the preparation and the reported endpoints are non-anthelmintic; retained activity does not identify an antiparasitic constituent

subject: A validated HPLC-UV method quantified santonin across A. cina extracts and leaves from eight Artemisia taxa, including A. absinthium
scope_note: supports lot- and species-specific santonin measurement and safety control; it is not a pooled abundance estimate or efficacy result

subject: Genome-wide analysis identified 24 AaOSC genes in CAS, LAS, LUS, and unknown subfamilies with differential expression under UV-B
scope_note: bioinformatic phylogeny and expression nominate triterpene candidates; they do not establish product identity, enzyme activity, or comparative copy-number evolution

subject: A new ent-kauranoid diterpene diglycoside and two known ent-kauranoid diterpenes were isolated from aerial material and structurally assigned by NMR
scope_note: structure-confirmed C20 chemistry expands class coverage; no antiparasitic endpoint or genus-wide distribution is established

subject: One new triterpene and four new lignans were isolated from aerial parts; reported cytotoxicity was compound- and cell-line-specific
scope_note: isolation confirms C30 chemical space but cytotoxicity is not antiparasitic efficacy or a native triterpene pathway assignment

subject: A new and a known triterpenoid saponin were isolated from whole-plant ethanol extract by spectroscopic methods
scope_note: structure-confirmed saponin evidence is specimen- and extraction-bounded and has no parasite or pathway-function evidence

subject: Two new nordammarane triterpenoids and two known cycloartane triterpenoids were isolated and showed alpha-glucosidase inhibition in vitro
scope_note: confirms nonvolatile C30 diversity in A. argyi; the enzyme endpoint does not establish antiparasitic activity or native biosynthetic flux

subject: Eight undescribed sesquiterpenoids and two undescribed triterpenoids, together with known analogues, were isolated and structurally characterized; one isolate reduced inflammatory signaling in macrophages
scope_note: broadens structure-confirmed class space and host-cell context but does not establish parasite activity or cross-species pathway homology

subject: Bio-guided isolation identified cinic acid; the isolated sesquiterpene was more active than the ethyl-acetate extract against Haemonchus contortus L3 infective larvae
scope_note: constituent-to-phenotype attribution is stronger than crude-extract evidence but requires host-selectivity, exposure, and target studies

subject: Dehydroleucodine isolated from aerial parts induced programmed cell-death phenotypes in Trypanosoma cruzi epimastigotes and trypomastigotes
scope_note: defined STL parasite activity does not identify a protein target, establish host selectivity, or transfer to wormwood

subject: HPLC profiling identified nine major phenolics; apigenin was the top predicted ligand for Leishmania N-myristoyltransferase in docking and molecular-dynamics analyses
scope_note: negative attribution control: apigenin is non-terpene and docking is not direct target engagement or parasite efficacy

subject: Hydrodistilled oils showed species-specific composition and activity against root-knot nematodes; A. absinthium oil was myrtenyl-acetate-rich whereas A. dracunculus oil was methyleugenol/beta-asarone-rich
scope_note: supports comparative chemotype dependence but oil mixtures, docking, and non-target effects prevent single-compound attribution

subject: Fractionated A. annua matrix components increased artemisinin exposure in a preclinical system; arteannuin B inhibited CYP3A4 in vitro
scope_note: supports a host-metabolism and matrix hypothesis, not a direct parasite-protein interaction or clinical botanical claim

subject: Haploid pseudo-chromosome assembly with approximately 4.2 Gbp genome size, 43,377 predicted genes, 91.37% complete BUSCOs, and 77.99% repetitive sequence
scope_note: adds a North American genome and repeat/ploidy context; no common annotation, terpene-family call, or parasite phenotype is inferred

subject: Resequenced A. tridentata genomes were compared with A. annua, revealing chromosomal rearrangements, conserved large-scale synteny, and population-level transposable-element differentiation
scope_note: supports genome-architecture and diploidization hypotheses but does not establish terpene-locus evolution or cross-species protein orthology

subject: Flow cytometry, chromosome counts, and reduced-representation sequencing supported one- and two-step WGD pathways, including a triploid bridge and a reported 0.22% polyploidization rate in the study material
scope_note: supports cytotype-aware sampling and evolutionary hypotheses; it is not a terpene-pathway or antiparasitic result

subject: A single 2 g/kg oral dose of ethanolic A. absinthium extract was less efficacious against naturally acquired caprine Eimeria coccidiosis than toltrazuril or amprolium; oocysts persisted to day 28
scope_note: negative or limited translation control for wormwood; crude-extract chemistry and dose optimization remain unresolved

subject: Alcoholic wormwood extracts were sampled at four phenological stages and quantified for alpha/beta-thujone by SPME-GC-MS plus absinthin, artemisetin, and dihydro-epi-deoxyarteannuin B by UHPLC-HR-MS
scope_note: supports harvest-stage and lot-specific chemical QC; it does not establish anthelmintic efficacy or a universal chemotype profile

subject: Across thujone-containing essential oils, multivariate analysis associated toxicity and behavior-modulating endpoints with multiple constituents rather than thujones alone
scope_note: supports mixture-aware risk assessment; rat and brine-shrimp endpoints do not define human exposure limits or vermifuge selectivity

subject: Two wormwood chemotypes were sampled in leaves and flowers across vegetative, budding, flowering, and post-flowering stages; flowers had higher oil content, while thujones and sabinyl acetate followed chemotype-specific trajectories
scope_note: supports tissue- and stage-matched chemical sampling; it does not predict anthelmintic activity or safety

subject: Eleven ex-situ Polish populations differed in oil content and 41-compound profiles, with sabinyl-acetate, mixed, and thujone chemotypes plus variable phenolic and tannin content
scope_note: supports within-species chemotype stratification and breeding/QC hypotheses; beginning-of-flowering and ex-situ context limit generalization

subject: A purified leaf protein converted arteannuin B to artemisinin with 58% conversion, Km 0.5 mM, and pH optimum 7.0–7.2 in the reported assay
scope_note: step-level biochemical evidence in A. annua; protein identity, native flux, and cross-species conservation require modern validation

subject: Across three growth stages and two seasons, davanone and linalool decreased while methyl/ethyl cinnamates, bicyclogermacrene, davana ether, 2-hydroxyisodavanone, and farnesol increased
scope_note: harvest-stage and season are required covariates; reported oil trends do not define antiparasitic activity

subject: Flow cytometry across 21 species and 24 populations found 2C DNA contents from 3.5 to 25.65 pg, with strong relationships to karyotype length and ploidy and additional ecological/systematic variation
scope_note: genome-size and ploidy context only; it does not infer terpene-gene copy number or chemistry

subject: Artemisinin concentration showed quantitative inheritance with predominant additive effects, high narrow-sense heritability, and selected hybrid lines reaching up to 1.4% in dry leaves
scope_note: breeding and within-species genetic association; causal loci and cross-environment stability remain unresolved

subject: Artemisinic acid was isolated from a hexane extract and its crystal structure was characterized as a possible biogenetic precursor of artemisinin
scope_note: structure and occurrence anchor only; isolation does not establish the complete in-planta conversion route or antiparasitic activity

subject: A Japanese wild-derived A. annua showed seasonal and positional variation in artemisinin, artemisinic acid, arteannuin B, and artemisitene, with leaf artemisinic acid reaching 1.0% dry weight
scope_note: accession-, site-, and year-specific chemistry; does not define a universal harvest optimum or causal environmental driver

subject: Salicylic acid treatment increased artemisinin, artemisinic acid, and dihydroartemisinic acid and was associated with an early ROS burst and selective pathway-gene responses
scope_note: elicitor and pathway-regulation evidence; does not establish field relevance, direct transcription-factor causality, or antiparasitic improvement

subject: A 1,151-bp CYP71AV1 promoter drove GUS expression in glandular secretory trichomes of young leaves and flower buds, shifted toward T-shaped trichomes in older leaves, and varied among varieties
scope_note: promoter-reporter localization and regulatory hypothesis; does not prove native protein abundance, flux, or cross-species promoter conservation

subject: RNAi knockdown of cinnamate-4-hydroxylase accumulated trans-cinnamic acid and salicylic acid and increased artemisinin while reducing phenylpropanoid outputs
scope_note: genetic perturbation supports cross-talk between phenylpropanoid/SA and artemisinin pathways; pleiotropy and native ecological relevance remain unresolved

subject: In-vitro shoot culture yielded the eudesmanolide artemin (2,5-dihydroxy-12,6-eudesmanolide-4(15)-ene), reported from this plant for the first time
scope_note: isolation-level STL occurrence; cancer-cell cytotoxicity is not antiparasitic activity or a therapeutic-window estimate

subject: Induced autotetraploid plants showed altered morphology, 8,763 differentially expressed genes, and higher mean artemisinin in the reported comparison
scope_note: ploidy-associated phenotype and transcriptome evidence; induction background, biomass tradeoffs, and causal genes require independent validation

subject: An α-thujone-rich A. sieberi oil containing α/β-thujone, camphor, and 1,8-cineole produced contact LC50 15.85 microgram/cm3 against adult Dermanyssus gallinae and retained residual toxicity for up to seven days
scope_note: mixture-level ectoparasite and repellent evidence; constituent causality, poultry safety, field performance, and human translation remain unresolved

subject: Artemisinin was measured at 0.20% summer and 0.14% autumn dry weight in A. sieberi, and an artemisinin-containing plant extract reduced severity/oocysts for Eimeria tenella and E. acervulina but not E. maxima
scope_note: species-, season-, extract-, and Eimeria-specific evidence; constituent exposure, host safety, and human malaria translation remain unresolved

subject: A. absinthium essential oils prepared by microwave-assisted processing, distillation in water, or direct steam distillation differed in acaricidal potency against Tetranychus urticae; direct-steam oil had LC50 0.04 mg/cm2 versus 0.13 mg/cm2 for the other methods and contained a candidate C15H24 sesquiterpene absent from those oils
scope_note: extraction- and mixture-specific ectoparasite evidence; the C15H24 feature is a candidate association, not causal identification or helminth/human evidence

subject: Activity-guided isolation from A. indica yielded exiguaflavones A and B, maackiain, and a benzofuran; exiguaflavones A/B inhibited Plasmodium falciparum in vitro
scope_note: useful non-terpene boundary/control for malaria review; does not support terpene activity or a genus-wide Artemisia mechanism

subject: A historical gelatin-capsule A. annua preparation was reported to clear parasitemia in P. berghei and P. vivax contexts, with high recrudescence reduced by longer or combined treatment in the reported study
scope_note: historical crude-preparation and metadata-limited evidence; no constituent attribution, modern quality control, or clinical efficacy inference

subject: Cold-induced AabHLH112 was highly expressed in glandular secretory trichomes, bound the AaERF1 promoter, and promoted artemisinin-pathway gene expression and artemisinin accumulation through ERF1-associated regulation
scope_note: plant regulatory evidence in A. annua; indirect regulation, native flux, cross-species conservation, and parasite potency remain untested

subject: ATAC-seq distinguished glandular-trichome and leaf accessible chromatin, with higher accessibility near DBR2 and CYP71AV1 in glandular trichomes and enrichment of regulatory motifs
scope_note: association-level epigenomic evidence; accessibility does not establish causal chromatin regulation, enzyme flux, or antiparasitic activity

subject: Aerial-part dichloromethane/methanol fractionation yielded a new monoterpene dimer, a known monoterpene, and three sesquiterpene lactones characterized by NMR and HRMS
scope_note: structure-confirmed chemical-space record; no antiparasitic endpoint or cross-species pathway inference

subject: Isolation of artemisinin-related terpenoids also recovered stigmasterol, friedelin, and friedelan-3-beta-ol, with friedelane-type triterpenoids reported from A. annua for the first time
scope_note: nonvolatile triterpene occurrence and cytotoxicity context; does not establish native abundance, pathway function, or parasite activity

subject: Supercritical CO2 extraction yielded 0.62-1.92% and produced artemisia ketone, camphor, 1,8-cineole, arteannuin B, and beta-selinene profiles that differed from hydrodistilled and steam-distilled oils
scope_note: method- and process-dependent chemistry; reported biological promise is not a parasite assay or single-constituent attribution

subject: Comparative plastome analysis across Artemisia species provides an infra-generic phylogenetic framework and highlights limited plastome sampling
scope_note: plastid phylogenetic context only; does not establish nuclear terpene-gene orthology, pathway evolution, or antiparasitic function

subject: Four partial genomic clones and two full-length cDNAs support a sesquiterpene-cyclase gene family; cASC34 and cASC125 showed transient and tissue-specific expression associated with flowering and high artemisinin concentration
scope_note: gene-family and expression evidence; the study does not assign products to the two cDNAs or establish cross-species orthology or parasite activity

subject: Recombinant CYP71AV1 oxidized amorpha-4,11-diene, artemisinic alcohol, and artemisinic aldehyde in yeast
scope_note: direct step-level pathway evidence in A. annua; does not establish native flux, terminal lactone formation, or conservation in another species

subject: Leaves and gland secretory cells contained oxygenated amorpha-diene intermediates, and enzyme activities supported a pathway from amorpha-4,11-diene through alcohol, aldehyde, and dihydroartemisinic acid
scope_note: hypothesized sequence integrates metabolite detection and enzyme activities; individual activities do not prove complete in-vivo flux or directionality

subject: A cyp71av1 mutant redirected sesquiterpene metabolism toward arteannuin X, which approached half the artemisinin concentration of wild type; isotope feeding supported nonenzymatic terminal steps
scope_note: genetic and isotope evidence for metabolic plasticity in A. annua; does not establish the same branch or flux in other Artemisia species

subject: Loss of a bornyl diphosphate synthase-associated locus reduced camphor and other monoterpenes while increasing FPP and several sesquiterpenes, but not artemisinin
scope_note: branch-competition and trichome-context evidence; engineered or segregating phenotype is not a universal natural tradeoff or antiparasitic mechanism

subject: HAP and LAP chemotypes differed in sesquiterpene accumulation and DBR2L expression; promoter variation, recombinant activity, and candidate regulatory elements were associated with artemisinin yield differences
scope_note: integrated omics and enzyme evidence in A. annua; promoter association does not prove causality, broad conservation, or a direct parasite phenotype

subject: An AaADS-homologous enzyme from A. maritima cyclized FPP to 4-amorphen-11-ol rather than amorpha-4,11-diene, and the product was made de novo in engineered yeast
scope_note: functional divergence among homologous TPS proteins; heterologous product formation is not native abundance, artemisinin production, or antiparasitic activity

subject: Helenalin, mexicanin, and dehydroleucodine inhibited cultured Leishmania mexicana promastigotes at estimated IC50 values of 2-4 micromolar and showed low mammalian-cell cytotoxicity in the reported study
scope_note: defined-compound phenotype with parasite-stage and host-cell boundaries; compound provenance is not a claim that all three are abundant in one Artemisia species

subject: A. absinthium oil contained camphor at 27.40% and inhibited promastigote and axenic-amastigote forms of L. aethiopica and L. donovani, with weak hemolysis and study-specific selectivity
scope_note: regional oil mixture and in-vitro evidence; camphor causality, standardized exposure, and human translation remain unresolved

subject: Methanolic, ether, and chloroform-derived A. sieberi aerial-part extracts reduced P. berghei parasitemia and reported no toxicity in the tested NMRI-mouse study
scope_note: whole-preparation murine evidence with unresolved active component, dose comparability, and human-malaria translation

subject: A flowering-stage A. khorassanica extract showed limited in-vivo activity against P. berghei; GC-MS identified chrysanthenone at 7.8% and cis-thujone at 5.8% among reported components
scope_note: species-, extraction-, and parasite-specific preparation evidence; composition is not proof that either volatile caused the phenotype

subject: Crude aqueous and ethanolic aerial-part extracts impaired adult Haemonchus contortus motility in vitro and reduced gastrointestinal-nematode fecal egg output in sheep; the ethanolic extract reached 90.46% FECR at 2.0 g/kg on day 15
scope_note: direct veterinary preparation evidence; extraction polarity and dose matter, while active terpene, standardized chemistry, residue, and human translation remain unresolved

subject: Aqueous wormwood extracts showed strong in-vitro H. contortus egg-hatch activity with ED50 1.40 mg/mL and ED99 3.76 mg/mL, but dry-wormwood dietary supplementation did not produce a significant group-level EPG reduction in experimentally infected lambs
scope_note: positive in-vitro/limited in-vivo translation boundary; mixed dietary chemistry and individual variability prevent terpene attribution

subject: In naturally infected Awassi sheep, a crude ethanolic A. absinthium extract at 1.0 g/kg produced 76.77% FECRT on day 15 versus 100% for albendazole, with no adverse effects observed during the small trial
scope_note: contemporary regional veterinary evidence; short follow-up, small sample, crude chemistry, and absent terpene exposure profiling limit efficacy and safety translation

subject: The 1.74-Gb highly heterozygous A. annua draft genome contained 63,226 predicted protein-coding genes; terpene-biosynthesis enzyme expansion and functional diversification were consistent with artemisinin-pathway evolution, and transcriptomics supported a regulatory network
scope_note: genome-scale evolutionary and pathway context; predicted gene expansion is not a direct cross-species copy-number, orthology, flux, or antiparasitic result

subject: A 3.89-Gb chromosome-scale A. argyi assembly on 17 pseudochromosomes supported a recent lineage-specific WGD, duplicated TPS expansion, germacrene-D/(+)-borneol/(+)-camphor pathway elucidation, and partial ADS deletion or homolog loss-of-function context
scope_note: assembly- and ploidy-specific comparative evidence; ADS absence and TPS expansion require common reannotation, homeolog-aware gene trees, expression, and enzyme validation

subject: Aerial parts yielded five new polyol monoterpenes and seven new sesquiterpene lactones, together with five previously identified compounds; structures were established by high-field NMR and one lactone by X-ray analysis
scope_note: specimen-bounded structural diversity in a Pacific Northwest species; no abundance denominator, pathway assignment, or antiparasitic endpoint

subject: Aerial-part extracts of A. giraldii var. giraldii, A. mongolica, and A. vestita contained sterols, alpha-amyrin, a new antifungal monoterpene santolinylol, and a new germacranolide among other constituents
scope_note: cross-species isolation and fungal bioassay anchor; antifungal activity is not helminth or malaria evidence, and detected compounds are not species-wide chemotype means

subject: A. igniaria extract contained four triterpenoids and additional long-chain esters and flavonoids; structures were determined spectroscopically, including first natural reports for beta-glutinanol and cis-p-coumaric acid eicosanyl ester
scope_note: extract- and specimen-bounded C30 evidence; no antiparasitic endpoint, pathway-gene assignment, or abundance generalization
